name: id-128-astral-characters
why: Zod 4 and Ajv 8 both count code points, so 128 astral characters fit a max(128).

name: id-129-astral-characters
why: One code point over. It is 258 UTF-16 units, which a validator counting units would also refuse, but for the wrong reason.

name: timestamp-arabic-indic-digits
why: The reason the generator rewrites \d to [0-9]: \d is Unicode decimal digits in Python and .NET, and these are decimal digits.

name: timestamp-lowercase-t
why: RFC 3339 permits a lowercase t; the generated pattern does not, and the pattern is the assertion.

name: timestamp-leap-second
why: RFC 3339 permits :60; the pattern caps seconds at 59.

name: timestamp-offset-without-colon
why: ISO 8601 basic format. The pattern requires the extended form.

name: timestamp-without-seconds
why: Seconds are not optional.

name: timestamp-twenty-digit-fraction
why: The fraction is unbounded in the pattern. Storage truncates it to milliseconds, which is a storage rule and not a validation one.

name: timestamp-positive-offset
why: An explicit offset is what the schema requires; it names the same instant as 16:31:02Z.

name: timestamp-negative-zero-offset
why: RFC 3339 gives -00:00 the meaning 'offset unknown'. The pattern accepts it and the server stores it as UTC.

name: duration-int4-maximum
why: 2^31 - 1, the largest value the int4 column holds.

name: duration-one-past-int4
why: 2^31. It passed the schema once and failed the insert, which a batch reported as a transient 500 the SDK resent forever.

name: duration-written-as-a-decimal
why: 5.0 is the number 5 to any JSON parser, so both validators call it an integer. A validator over arbitrary-precision numbers would not.

name: process-id-beyond-the-safe-integer-range
why: 9007199254740993 parses to 9007199254740992, one past the maximum the generator emits. Senders are told to write integers beyond 2^53 as strings.

name: unknown-top-level-field
why: Accepted rather than refused, which is what makes an additive optional field a compatible change. It is not stored and not hashed (ADR-049).

name: proto-key-in-aliases
why: Accepted by both validators, and kept by the parser since parseEnvelope restores it.

name: proto-key-in-metadata
why: The same, for the other record field.

name: proto-key-in-aliases-with-a-non-string-value
why: z.record neither validates nor keeps this key, so restoring it unchecked would put an object into a field encryption expects to be a string.

name: unsupported-protocol-version
why: Checked before the event, which is where unsupported_protocol_version comes from. The composed envelope schema is what makes Ajv agree.

name: missing-event
why: The envelope requires it.

name: null-event
why: Present and unusable. z.unknown() accepts null in the envelope, and the event schema refuses it.

name: event-is-an-array
why: A batch body sent to the single-event route looks like this.

name: empty-error-message
why: An error with nothing in it is worse than no error: it marks the journey failed and says nothing.

name: non-string-alias-value
why: Aliases are identifiers, and every one is encrypted and tokenized as text.

name: journeyId-at-maximum
why: 128 characters, the most the schema allows. The pair exists so the over-maximum case below cannot pass because everything is refused.

name: journeyId-over-maximum
why: One character past 128. A generated schema that lost this maxLength would accept it while Zod refuses, which is the divergence this file exists to catch.

name: journey-label-200-astral-characters
why: 200 code points, the most a label may hold. They are 400 UTF-16 units, so a validator counting units would refuse what the contract accepts.

name: journey-label-empty
why: An empty label is refused rather than read as clearing the label; a host that wants no label sends none.

name: journey-label-not-a-string
